To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the recently-introduced class ODE-Nets establishes a fruitful connection to dynamical systems; (2) the weights of ODE-Nets can be formulated using continuous-in-depth functions, and (3) this view allows us, among other things, to leverage parameter transformations, and to formulate a novel ODE-Block with statefulness that can be applied to both image classification and sentence-tagging tasks

1) the recently introduced class of ordinary differential equations networks (ODE-Net) can be reformulated to incorporate continuous-in-depth functions; 2) this reformulation enables the incorporation of meaningful stateful layers, such as batch normalization, into ODE-Nets; 3) the reformulated ODE-Nets can be compressed without retraining through a change of continuous-in-depth basis functions

(a) the weights of ODE-Nets are best formulated as continuous-in-depth linear combinations of basis function; (b) the stateful ODE-Network is a novel architecture that enables incorporating continuous-in-depth batch norm layers to achieve state of the art performance; and (c) the stateful architecture enables compressing the network weights without retraining, reducing inference time and memory usage
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (a) a stateful ODE block, (b) a novel formulation of weights as a linear combination of basis functions, (c) a method to compress weights without retraining using a change of basis and (d) a method to incorporate continuous-in-depth batch norm into ODE-Nets.

the following contributions: (a) a novel stateful continuous-in-depth ODE-Block formulation; (b) a novel continuous-in-depth batch-normalization layer; (c) a novel weight compression technique based on a change of basis; (d) a new state-of-the-art ResNet-50 model for image classification.

the development of novel ODE-Blocks that are (a) stateful, (b) enable the inclusion of batch normalization layers, and (c) can be compressed through a change of the weight basis without retraining, thereby achieving state-of-the-art results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have proposed an ODE-Block formulation that allows for the inclusion of stateful layers and a change of basis for compression.
we introduce a novel ODE-Block formulation which enables the use of continuous-in-depth batch norm and allows for weight compression.

we propose a novel stateful formulation of ODE-Nets that allows us to incorporate continuous-in-depth batch normalizations layers to achieve state of the art performance, while also allowing us to compress the weights through a simple change of basis, while still maintaining near state of the art accuracy and reducing both inference-time and memory footprint.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stateful ODE-Networks can be formulated as a general class of dynamical systems, and that they can benefit from the rich literature on parameter transformations.
we show that the ODE-Block can be stateful, and we show that the weights of the ODE-Blocks can be reduced through parameter transformations.
we propose a novel stateful formulation for ODE-Blocks that allows for incorporating stateful batch normalization layers and compressing the weights of an ODE-Net without retraining.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stateful layers are not only useful but also essential in the context of ODE-Blocks, as they enable the use of continuous-in-depth batch normalizations.
ODE-Nets, when viewed through a continuous-in-depth lens, can be used to formulate stateful layers that are more expressive and can be compressed to reduce computational and memory costs.
continuous-in-depth functions can be leveraged to improve ODE-Net architectures and to compress the weights of deep learning networks.
